identity.title: Cross-Domain Lossy Compression via Rate- and Classification-Constrained Optimal Transport

problem.claim: The paper studies lossy compression where the encoder observes a degraded source but the decoder reconstructs samples from a distinct target distribution.

contributions.claim: It formulates cross-domain lossy compression as constrained optimal transport with rate and classification-loss constraints.

It derives closed-form DRC/RDC tradeoffs for Bernoulli sources with Hamming distortion, analytic DRC/RDC expressions for Gaussian models with mean-squared error, and DRPC functions incorporating KL and squared-Wasserstein perception divergences.
It develops deep end-to-end models for super-resolution, denoising, and inpainting across the listed datasets to compare empirical performance with the theoretical results.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state a unified constrained-transport framework that jointly incorporates compression rate, classification loss, and, in its extension, perception divergences for cross-domain lossy compression.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that shared common randomness reduces the one-shot setting to a deterministic transport plan and enables closed-form Bernoulli DRC/RDC tradeoffs under Hamming distortion.
The authors report analytic DRC/RDC expressions for Gaussian models in the asymptotic regime under mean-squared error.
The authors report consistency between theoretical results and empirical performance in models for super-resolution, denoising, and inpainting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines cross-domain lossy compression with degraded-source encoding and target-distribution reconstruction.
Casts the task as constrained optimal transport with rate and classification-loss constraints.
Derives one-shot Bernoulli and asymptotic Gaussian tradeoff expressions under specified distortions.
Adds KL and squared-Wasserstein perception divergences and derives DRPC functions.
Reports end-to-end experiments across super-resolution, denoising, and inpainting tasks and datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract introduces a constrained-transport formulation, specializes it to tractable Bernoulli and Gaussian cases, then extends it with perception divergences before reporting application experiments.

lessons.interpretation: A layered presentation can connect a general formulation to interpretable special cases and broader constraints before empirical testing.
lessons.application: Structure a paper by stating the general constrained problem, deriving at least one transparent special case, extending the constraint set, and then mapping experiments to those theoretical claims.
lessons.exception: This sequence may be unsuitable when the target problem lacks tractable special cases or when theory and experiments do not share comparable metrics.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact tradeoff formulas, model architectures, baselines, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
The reported empirical consistency is not quantified, and the abstract does not establish whether the framework improves over competing approaches.
